answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with bonded identity escrow: every agent locks a refundable stake before it may trade, like timber stacked as collateral on a terrace above a frozen tundra of fake accounts. Random audits challenge agents to complete real work; a failure or a duplicated answer slashes the bond. An attacker spawning a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand bonds, and each caught fake burns its stake, so the cost of a sybil farm grows linearly while honest agents simply get their bond back.
